VOIL — Vehicle Identification & Overview
What is VOIL? Vehicle Overview & Identification Logs — required on every claim. These shots prove the vehicle matches the policy and set the baseline before any work begins.
1
VIN — Door Plate
Clear close-up of the door jamb sticker — full 17 chars visible
req
2
VIN — Through Windshield
Shoot from outside through the glass at the dash VIN plate
req
3
Odometer
Key on, engine off — capture full mileage reading
req
4
Instrument Panel
Full cluster visible — shows warning lights & gauges
req
5
Interior (2–3 photos)
Front seats, rear seats, and cargo area — show overall condition
req
6
License Plate
Straight-on, legible — include state and expiration sticker
req
7
Four Corners (1 photo)
One walk-around shot from each corner — establishes full vehicle

CONDITIONING — Potential Total Loss
When to shoot COND Trigger at 50%+ of ACV. These photos document the vehicle's overall condition to support the estimate and valuation — tires, engine, interior, and trim.
1
Tire FL — Setup + Gauge
Full tire visible + tread depth gauge reading (2 pics)
req

Full tire visible + tread depth gauge reading (2 pics)
req

Full tire visible + tread depth gauge reading (2 pics)

Full tire visible + tread depth gauge reading (2 pics)

Engine Compartment — Top Down
Hood open, shoot straight down — show belts, fluid levels, hoses

Underneath Front Engine — Ground Up
Shoot up from ground level — show leaks, rust, undercarriage
req

Interior Condition Set (4+ photos)
This is the final free-shoot set. Keep shooting until you've covered the main areas below, then add extras anywhere you need more detail.
Door Panels Seats / All Rows Headliner / Sunroof Dashboard
4+
8
Options / CPE / Refurbishments
One combined bucket for aftermarket upgrades, tint, wheels, accessories, and other value-adding items. Add as many photos as needed.
UPD — Unrelated Prior Damage
Why UPD matters Protects both the tech and the estimate. Pre-existing damage that isn't documented could be blamed on the repair — shoot everything that was there before you started.
All Pre-Existing Damage
Walk around the vehicle — photograph every scratch, ding, dent, or damage not related to this claim. Setup shot + close-up for each.
SCOPE — Storm Damage
Scope = the core claim This is the heart of the documentation. Photograph every storm-damaged panel with a setup shot + close-up. Glass damage needs both an exterior and interior shot.
Storm Damage — Panel by Panel
Photograph every damaged panel. For each: one setup shot showing the full panel, then close-ups of individual dents/impacts.
Glass Damage (if applicable)
Setup pic of each damaged glass piece, plus a close-up showing crack/chip detail from both sides.
